page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features 192 dedicated vCPUs derived from 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. System resources include 768 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and accelerated cryptography primitives. The instance does not include bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight high-throughput parallel compute capabilities, placing multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics in the top tier. Measured memory throughput shows uncached read bandwidth reaching 510.75 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 215.02 GB/sec. Application testing reveals strong throughput in data processing, logging 173.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 188.19 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, single-thread performance scores in the middle tier, demonstrating that workload efficiency relies on multi-threaded parallel execution. The absence of local disk drives requires provisioning network-attached block storage for persistence.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the D192s_v6 provides massive compute density per host node, reducing infrastructure management overhead for large-scale enterprise deployments compared to fleets of smaller instances. It is suitable for highly parallel tasks including in-memory caching fleets, relational and NoSQL database engines, extensive continuous integration pipelines, batch analytics, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D192s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Configured with 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores and 768 GB of memory, it delivers a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance features advanced hardware instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, with 260 MB of shared L3 cache. It lacks integrated local storage and GPU hardware, depending on external storage for persistent state. Benchmark metrics demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by 173.14 million Redis SET operations per second and high aggregate memory read bandwidth of 510.75 GB/sec, offset by moderate single-core throughput. Providing extensive resource consolidation without discrete acceleration overhead, the D192s_v6 is engineered for large-scale in-memory databases, parallel batch processing, high-concurrency web serving, and CPU-bound analytical workloads.
